implementationScope: package-only progressive JFIF 4:2:0 incremental session with semantic-unit transport, dynamic pre-SOF table ownership, SOF ownership-transfer into dynamic frame quantization slots, first-SOS DQT release, actual-only coefficient planes, exact current post-SOF Huffman payloads and validated-EOI final-ready compaction

cases.mechanismPressure: two 64-byte DQT payloads are allocated before SOF2, transferred by pointer ownership into the frame quantization store, survive pre-SOS redefinition authority, and are released at first SOS without ever materializing a four-slot fixed frame arena
large coefficient/render phases stay unchanged while the two actual DQT payloads move across SOF2 without copy coexistence; the 256-byte future frame-q authority remains admission-only
DQT ownership transfer composes with later restart-heavy MCU rollback and split marker suspension without changing final RGB or transaction scratch

requiredInvariants: All v11 transport, pre-frame table ownership, source semantics, first-SOS quantization latch, actual coefficient geometry, dynamic Huffman, preview backing, restart and EOI-compaction invariants remain unchanged.

FrameQuantizationSourceState no longer allocates one fixed four-slot arena. Each frame DQT selector owns one 64-byte payload only while present; the maximum future frame-q authority is exactly 256 bytes.

At SOF2, pre-frame DQT payload pointers are transferred into FrameQuantizationSourceState rather than copied. The same physical semantic payload therefore changes authority/lifetime without a duplicate 64-byte allocation.
Pre-frame DHT definitions, if present, are still installed into the post-SOF dynamic Huffman store because their representation/lifetime differs. Only DQT ownership is transferred directly.

All three retained sources own exactly DQT0 and DQT1 before SOF2. Their pre-frame table high-water and frame-q high-water are both exactly 128 bytes; neither stage materializes absent DQT2/DQT3 capacity.

DQT redefinition remains legal between SOF2 and first SOS. A newly introduced selector during that phase may grow frame-q current ownership up to the 256-byte maximum. DQT after first SOS remains fail closed.
First SOS still binds the selected source quantizers into three component dequantization tables and releases all frame-q payloads. Final-ready retainedFrameQuantizationSourceBytes is exactly zero.

Because DQT ownership is transferred rather than copied, the SOF transition maximum does not add a separate frameQuantizationSourceByteCount term on top of initial maximum pre-frame authority and persistent maximum state. Schemas 7 through 11 retain their historical coexistence formula; schema12 deliberately changes it.

The post-SOF/pre-DHT tiny witness at byte prefix 177 retains exactly 2398 bytes: 414 transport + 1856 persistent base state + 128 transferred DQT payloads. Pre-frame current ownership is zero at that point.

The maximum pre-frame authority remains 2432 bytes and actual initial retained state remains 414 bytes; the maximum frame-q authority remains 256 bytes. Corpus high-water values must not narrow those admission bounds.

Final-ready retained values remain RGB-only as in v10/v11: tiny 897 bytes, noise576 995328 bytes, restart64 12288 bytes. Operation peaks remain 8095, 2010910 and 30494 bytes because render phases dominate the slightly lower SOF-transition term.

This profile does not qualify malloc headers, allocator size classes, Swift object/pointer fields, physical RSS, non-JFIF semantics, embedded ICC, other sampling modes or perceptual reconstruction quality.
